title: Mirror Tree
statement:
Flip a binary tree left to right by rewiring its existing nodes.

Contract
- `root` may be null. Nodes have an integer `value` and mutable `left` and `right` references.
- At every node, swap the left and right children, then return the root. Mutate the nodes you are given: do not allocate replacement nodes or change values.
- The returned root is the same node that was passed in; a null tree returns null.
- Trees may be lopsided, with a height of up to 1000 nodes.

Examples
- `[5, 2, 8, 1, null, 7, 9]` becomes `[5, 8, 2, 9, 7, null, 1]`.
- `[1, 2]` becomes `[1, null, 2]`.
- A null tree stays null.
hints: Mirroring a tree means every node trades its two children, not just the root.
Swap the two child references of the current node, then mirror what is now each child. A null child needs no work.

Every node is touched once. Intended complexity: O(n) time for n nodes. Space is the recursion depth: O(h) for tree height h, which is O(log n) for a balanced tree (the workload uses balanced trees) and O(n) for a chain.
inputSyntax: Input: the tree in level order with null for missing children, for example: [5, 2, 8, 1, null, 7, 9]
